tables.name: medical_cases
tables.purpose: One recovery episode. Injury and illness share the record; only injury creates a booking hold. Claim tracking is independent of clearance.

fields.name: id
fields.rule: Required; generated by server.

fields.name: workerId
fields.rule: Required; worker whose recovery is tracked.

fields.name: companyId
fields.rule: Originating business. Optional for an off-shift report with no business; never use this to limit the worker-wide injury hold.

fields.name: kind
fields.rule: INJURY | ILLNESS. Conversion changes ILLNESS to INJURY in place; never copies documents.

fields.name: workRelated
fields.rule: Required; default false pending confirmation. Only work-related injuries require claim tracking.

fields.name: status
fields.rule: AWAITING_NOTE | RECOVERING | PENDING_REVIEW | RESOLVED | VOIDED. No SHARED status: sharing and medical clearance are separate.

fields.name: incidentDate
fields.rule: Required; local occurrence date. A cancellation starts an illness episode on its local shift date.

fields.name: reportedAt
fields.rule: Required; time first accepted into case tracking.

fields.name: expectedRtwDate
fields.rule: Current worker-reported expected return date. Projection of the latest applicable submission; never proof of clearance.

fields.name: reviewDueAt
fields.rule: Set when a full-clearance submission is pending; one business day under the configured Ops calendar.

fields.name: followUpCycle
fields.rule: Default 0; increment on each new submission, conversion, resolution, or void to invalidate stale follow-ups.

fields.name: version
fields.rule: Default 1; compare-and-set version for concurrent Ops/worker commands.

fields.name: approvedSubmissionId
fields.rule: Set only on injury approval. Must reference a FULL submission of this case.

fields.name: resolvedAt
fields.rule: Required exactly when RESOLVED; injury approval resolves immediately in v1.

fields.name: voidedAt
fields.rule: Required exactly when VOIDED; false reports only.

fields.name: closeReason
fields.rule: Ops resolution/void reason. Closing an unresponsive injury cannot bypass the clearance rule.

fields.name: claimStatus
fields.rule: NOT_REQUIRED | NOT_FILED | FILED | UNDER_REVIEW | APPROVED | DENIED | CLOSED. Default NOT_REQUIRED; confirmed work-related injury starts NOT_FILED.

fields.name: claimNumber
fields.rule: Carrier claim identifier; not a LegalClaim id.

fields.name: carrier
fields.rule: Carrier name; no carrier API integration in v1.

fields.name: claimFiledAt
fields.rule: When insurance filing occurred; required once the claim is marked FILED or later.

fields.name: openedByType
fields.rule: WORKER | OPS | NEUTRON | SYSTEM; authenticated server attribution.

fields.name: openedByInternalUserId
fields.rule: Required only for an Ops actor; Neutron attribution is in the event timeline.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.rule: Required; server time at creation.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.rule: Required; server time on each update.

constraints: Index (workerId, kind, status) for medical holds; (status, reviewDueAt) for queue/SLA; (companyId, reportedAt) for origin filters.
An INJURY needs a linked, confirmed Incident. An ILLNESS needs at least one linked cancelled WorkerShift.
Claim fields may change after medical resolution. They never reopen the hold.

ILLNESS starts RECOVERING. A worker recovery confirmation or explicit Ops close resolves it; an expected date alone never proves medical clearance. No-date illness adds no injury reminder cycle. INJURY starts AWAITING_NOTE; NOT_CLEARED/RESTRICTED inputs become RECOVERING; FULL becomes PENDING_REVIEW.
RESOLVED injury requires same-case approved FULL submission; VOIDED requires explicit Ops permission and reason. No automatic 30-day close.

Reference targets must belong to the case worker. Use RESTRICT for case/document history; actor FKs may SET NULL while events retain actor snapshots. Final retention/deletion policy is a product decision.
tables.relationships: workers 1:N medical_cases; companies 1:N origin cases; medical_cases 1:N incidents, submissions, events, affected shifts, notices, and effects.

tables.name: medical_submissions
tables.purpose: Immutable worker input and optional private document; Ops review metadata is updated separately. Repeated notes are separate rows.

fields.name: id
fields.rule: Required; generated.

fields.name: caseId
fields.rule: Required.

fields.name: clientRequestId
fields.rule: Required; worker app retains the same id on retry.

fields.name: submittedByWorkerId
fields.rule: Required; must equal case.workerId.

fields.name: documentFilePath
fields.rule: Private medical_documents object key, not a public URL. Required for injury submissions; optional for illness.

fields.name: originalFileName
fields.rule: Required when a document is present.

fields.name: mimeType
fields.rule: Required with document; JPEG, PNG, HEIC converted to JPEG, or PDF after server validation.

fields.name: fileSizeBytes
fields.rule: Required with document; positive, within configured size cap.

fields.name: visitDate
fields.rule: Required for injury, optional for illness; cannot be in the future.

fields.name: clearanceType
fields.rule: FULL | RESTRICTED | NOT_CLEARED; required for an injury note, null allowed for illness.

fields.name: expectedRtwDate
fields.rule: Required for non-FULL injury inputs when known. An explicit unknown date is allowed and schedules a 14-day check-in; a past date is rejected.

fields.name: returnDateUnknown
fields.rule: Default false. Non-FULL injury requires exactly one of expectedRtwDate or explicit unknown=true; FULL input uses false. Unknown schedules the 14-day check-in.

fields.name: liftingLimitLb
fields.rule: Positive lifting limit; null means no supplied lifting restriction.

fields.name: standingLimitHours
fields.rule: Positive standing limit, at most 24 hours.

fields.name: noRepetitiveMotion
fields.rule: Default false; worker-reported structured restriction.

fields.name: noHeights
fields.rule: Default false; covers ladders/heights.

fields.name: noMachinery
fields.rule: Default false.

fields.name: restrictionsNote
fields.rule: Other restrictions; private to worker and injury-authorized Ops.

fields.name: workerNote
fields.rule: Optional worker context; never placed in the customer notice payload.

fields.name: reviewStatus
fields.rule: NOT_REQUIRED | PENDING | APPROVED | REJECTED | INFO_REQUESTED. FULL injury notes start PENDING; recovery/illness inputs start NOT_REQUIRED.

fields.name: reviewedByInternalUserId
fields.rule: Required for a review decision.

fields.name: reviewedAt
fields.rule: Set on review decision.

fields.name: reviewReason
fields.rule: Required for Reject or Request info; worker-visible explanation.

fields.name: submittedAt
fields.rule: Required; server timestamp.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.rule: Changes only with review metadata.

constraints: Unique (caseId, clientRequestId); index (caseId, submittedAt) and (reviewStatus, submittedAt).
File metadata is all present or all absent. The object must have been uploaded by this worker to this case namespace; verify ownership before attaching.
Illness submission needs at least one of document, expected date, or worker note. FULL injury input cannot simultaneously assert active restrictions.
Approve applies only to the newest pending FULL submission. Stale review commands fail on case version; never overwrite a newer restricted note.
Keep submissions immutable; corrections and reuploads create new rows. Store dates as dates, not midnight UTC.
tables.relationships: Each row belongs to one medical_case and one submitting worker. Events, shift effects, approvals, and illness document consents can reference it.

tables.name: medical_case_events
tables.purpose: Append-only case history for humans and machines. It records decisions, input provenance, and effect outcomes.

fields.name: id
fields.rule: Required.

fields.name: caseId
fields.rule: Required.

fields.name: submissionId
fields.rule: Submission being acted on, if any.

fields.name: sequence
fields.rule: Monotonic within a case; allocated while holding the case lock.

fields.name: eventType
fields.rule: CASE_OPENED | REPORT_LINKED | SUBMISSION_RECEIVED | REVIEW_DECIDED | CLAIM_UPDATED | CONVERTED_TO_INJURY | CASE_VOIDED | EFFECT_COMPLETED | EFFECT_FAILED | NOTICE_SENT | CONSENT_CHANGED.

fields.name: actorType
fields.rule: WORKER | OPS | NEUTRON | SYSTEM.

fields.name: actorInternalUserId
fields.rule: Ops actor, when applicable.

fields.name: actorWorkerId
fields.rule: Worker actor, when applicable.

fields.name: actorLabel
fields.rule: Server-authenticated attribution snapshot, such as Ops email or named agent; survives account removal.

fields.name: payload
fields.rule: Typed payload per event: previous/next state, ids, decision and reason. Private; no signed URLs or document bytes.

fields.name: idempotencyKey
fields.rule: Stable command/event key; prevents duplicate history on retry.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.rule: Required; immutable.

constraints: Unique (caseId, sequence), unique idempotencyKey; index (caseId, createdAt).
Event and case changes are committed together. Events are not an alternative source of live state.
Actor identity comes from auth, never from submitted body fields. Do not expose full events to business users.
tables.relationships: medical_cases 1:N events; submissionId optionally points to the note behind the decision. Effects reference the triggering event.

tables.name: medical_case_shifts
tables.purpose: Which worker shifts a case affected, why, and whether cancellation or medical exemption completed. Supports multiple cases affecting one shift.

fields.name: id
fields.rule: Required.

fields.name: caseId
fields.rule: Required.

fields.name: workerShiftId
fields.rule: Required; must belong to case.workerId.

fields.name: submissionId
fields.rule: Input selecting this shift; null for initial 48-hour policy.

fields.name: selectionReason
fields.rule: INITIAL_48H | RECOVERY_WINDOW | LATER_SHIFT_REVIEW | ILLNESS_ORIGIN | WORKER_OPTED_IN.

fields.name: impactStatus
fields.rule: CANCEL_REQUESTED | CANCELLED | REVIEW_REQUIRED | KEPT_IN_PROGRESS | REVIEW_RELEASED | CANCEL_FAILED. Persist actual outcomes, not assumptions.

fields.name: exemptionStatus
fields.rule: NONE | REQUESTED | APPLIED | FAILED. Medical penalty exemption is independent from cancellation completion.

fields.name: cancelledAt
fields.rule: Successful cancellation timestamp copied from the pipeline result.

fields.name: exemptionAppliedAt
fields.rule: When the existing penalty/strike correction completed.

fields.name: lastErrorCode
fields.rule: Actionable cancellation or exemption error, without medical detail.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.rule: Required; server time at creation.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.rule: Required; server time on each update.

constraints: Unique (caseId, workerShiftId); index workerShiftId and (caseId, impactStatus).
Do not recancel an already-cancelled shift. A second case adds another association and reuses the actual shift result.
Resolving or voiding a case releases review flags; it never rebooks cancelled shifts or deletes historical exemptions.
Known RTW date includes shifts whose local start date is on/before that date. Initial window is [case accepted time, accepted time + 48 elapsed hours). Exclude started shifts; alert Ops instead.
tables.relationships: Join between medical_cases and worker_shifts; worker_shifts already links workers and shifts. Notice shift lists are filtered to the recipient company.

tables.name: medical_case_notices
tables.purpose: An Ops-previewed, safe customer notice and its delivery record. One row per recipient; a medical clearance can exist before its notice is sent.

fields.name: id
fields.rule: Required.

fields.name: caseId
fields.rule: Required.

fields.name: companyId
fields.rule: Required; recipient business, which may differ from originating business for another affected shift.

fields.name: recipientUserId
fields.rule: Known business recipient if available.

fields.name: recipientEmail
fields.rule: Required; server-resolved/confirmed recipient snapshot.

fields.name: noticeKind
fields.rule: ABSENCE | CLEARANCE.

fields.name: safePayload
fields.rule: Allowlisted snapshot: worker display name, company-scoped affected shift ids/labels, expected return or cleared date, and illness note-on-file boolean.

fields.name: subject
fields.rule: Template-rendered safe subject.

fields.name: bodyText
fields.rule: Template-rendered body; no arbitrary medical free text or note attachment.

fields.name: status
fields.rule: DRAFT | QUEUED | SENT | FAILED | AMBIGUOUS. DRAFT is private to Ops; customer read model includes SENT only.

fields.name: previewedByInternalUserId
fields.rule: Ops user who previewed the current content.

fields.name: previewedAt
fields.rule: Any edit invalidates this stamp; send requires current preview.

fields.name: queuedByInternalUserId
fields.rule: Authenticated Ops actor requesting send.

fields.name: queuedAt
fields.rule: Set atomically with SEND_CUSTOMER_NOTICE effect.

fields.name: sentAt
fields.rule: Provider-accepted delivery timestamp; not a promise that an email was read.

fields.name: providerMessageId
fields.rule: Provider acknowledgement used for reconciliation.

fields.name: idempotencyKey
fields.rule: Stable case/event/recipient key; repeated Send clicks do not enqueue another notice.

fields.name: lastErrorCode
fields.rule: Delivery failure/ambiguity.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.rule: Required; server time at creation.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.rule: Required; server time on each update.

constraints: Index (companyId, status, sentAt) for business read model; (caseId, createdAt) for case history.
Approval removes only the medical hold. Sending is a separate explicit Ops action after preview; failed send does not re-block the worker.
Do not send a 'can return' notice if another open injury or account restriction still prevents work. Recheck overall eligibility at send time.
For illness, confirmation that a note is on file does not grant access to the file. No injury documents are exposed to business users.
tables.relationships: Case 1:N notices; recipient belongs to users/company scope. A SEND_CUSTOMER_NOTICE effect references noticeId; the business console consumes a redacted notice projection.

tables.name: medical_document_consents
tables.purpose: Explicit, revocable permission for one illness document to one business. Default is private; injury documents cannot be shared in v1.

fields.name: id
fields.rule: Required.

fields.name: submissionId
fields.rule: Required; submission must have a document and currently belong to an illness case.

fields.name: companyId
fields.rule: Required; exact business receiving document access.

fields.name: grantedByWorkerId
fields.rule: Required; authenticated owner of the submission.

fields.name: grantedAt
fields.rule: Required; server time after affirmative in-app consent.

fields.name: expiresAt
fields.rule: Optional expiry; expiry period awaits policy decision.

fields.name: revokedAt
fields.rule: Set on worker revoke or illness-to-injury conversion.

fields.name: consentTextVersion
fields.rule: Exact consent copy/version shown to worker.

fields.name: clientRequestId
fields.rule: Stable request id for retry-safe grant.

constraints: Partial unique (submissionId, companyId) WHERE revokedAt IS NULL; expired grants must be revoked before a replacement.
Each new document needs its own grant; no case-wide boolean that silently shares later uploads.

Business file endpoint rechecks worker ownership, company membership, active consent, expiry, and current case kind on every request, then streams privately with Cache-Control: no-store. Do not expose reusable signed storage URLs to businesses.
Revocation prevents new downloads. It cannot retract a file already downloaded; the consent copy must say that.
tables.relationships: medical_submissions 1:N consent history; each grant references one worker and one company. Conversion revokes all active consents in the same transaction.

tables.name: medical_case_effects
tables.purpose: Small transactional outbox and durable action schedule. Existing jobs, cancellation, outreach, and todos execute these actions; no new messaging or scheduler platform.

fields.name: id
fields.rule: Required; use as downstream idempotency identity.

fields.name: caseId
fields.rule: Required.

fields.name: triggerEventId
fields.rule: Required; case event that requested the action.

fields.name: noticeId
fields.rule: Required for customer send.

fields.name: workerShiftId
fields.rule: Required for cancel/exemption actions.

fields.name: effectType
fields.rule: CANCEL_SHIFT | APPLY_MEDICAL_EXEMPTION | WORKER_MESSAGE | FOLLOW_UP | OPS_CALL_TASK | REVIEW_SLA | CLAIM_REMINDER | SEND_CUSTOMER_NOTICE.

fields.name: payload
fields.rule: Validated typed payload with ids, template keys and date parameters; no medical files or free text for customer actions.

fields.name: dueAt
fields.rule: Required; immediate actions use now; future follow-ups use local morning converted to UTC.

fields.name: followUpCycle
fields.rule: Required for follow-up/review jobs; execution skips stale cycle or state.

fields.name: status
fields.rule: PENDING | RUNNING | COMPLETE | RETRY | CANCELLED | FAILED | AMBIGUOUS.

fields.name: dedupeKey
fields.rule: case/event/action/target identity. Create once, retry the same row.

fields.name: attemptCount
fields.rule: Default 0; increment on lease acquisition.

fields.name: leaseUntil
fields.rule: Claim timeout; reclaim expired leases for safe actions.

fields.name: nextAttemptAt
fields.rule: Backoff for retryable failure.

fields.name: scheduledJobId
fields.rule: Existing JobsScheduler Firestore job id; payload names effectId.

fields.name: outreachAttemptId
fields.rule: Existing broker attempt when this is worker outreach.

fields.name: workerTodoId
fields.rule: Existing Ops call/review task.

fields.name: externalRef
fields.rule: Non-DB provider acknowledgement for reconciliation.

fields.name: lastErrorCode
fields.rule: Failure code; actionable in Ops.

fields.name: completedAt
fields.rule: Required when COMPLETE.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.rule: Required; server time at creation.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.rule: Required; server time on each update.

constraints: Index (status, dueAt), (status, nextAttemptAt), (caseId, followUpCycle).
Commit case, event and effects together. Dispatcher reads due rows with leases and schedules/executes via existing services.
Retry-safe cancellation/exemption rereads actual shift state. Outreach uses effectId as sourceId and a dedicated registered medical type.
Provider send ambiguity becomes AMBIGUOUS for reconciliation; do not promise exactly-once email delivery without provider idempotency.
Old follow-up cycles are skipped at execution even if an already-created job cannot be cancelled. Bounded retries end in a visible FAILED action and Ops task.
tables.relationships: Case 1:N effects, each tied to an event. Optional joins to existing outreach_attempts, worker_todos and worker_shifts. Jobs remain in the existing Firestore jobs collection.

existing.name: incidents
existing.change: Add nullable medicalCaseId FK → medical_cases.id and nullable sourceReference. Add a partial unique (source, sourceReference) index when a reference is present.
existing.why: Reuse worker/supervisor/Ops intake and report evidence. Several confirmed reports can attach to one case; unconfirmed reports remain unattached in PENDING_CONFIRMATION. Keep one incident per actual report, rather than discarding duplicate evidence.

existing.name: worker_shifts + CancellationCategory
existing.change: Add MEDICAL to CancellationCategory. WorkerShift scalar fields stay as-is; add only the reverse medical_case_shifts relation.
existing.why: Use existing cancellation source/reason/category fields and the existing strike correction path. Keep attribution accurate: system/Ops-triggered cancellations are not worker-initiated; late illness uploads can change exemption without recancelling.

existing.name: workers + account_status
existing.change: No Injured column and no account-status rewrite. Add a derived medicalHold/medicalTask projection to worker API responses.
existing.why: hasMedicalHold = EXISTS INJURY case with status AWAITING_NOTE, RECOVERING or PENDING_REVIEW. Booking is allowed only if existing eligibility also passes. Clearing a case never unsuspends the worker.

existing.name: outreach_attempts + worker_todos + existing jobs
existing.change: Register medical outreach type/source and job payload {effectId}; reuse existing ids and attribution. Add medical-specific todo category/source conventions.
existing.why: Existing broker owns SMS/push preferences, suppression, deduplication and audit. WorkerTodo represents the Ops task; it is not assumed to be the worker app home card.

existing.name: claims + legal_claims + worker_uploads
existing.change: Keep existing records. No new injury LegalClaim is auto-created. Medical files use a dedicated namespace and submission ownership rather than generic worker document links.
existing.why: Legal case management and insurance filing are distinct. Reuse storage/transcoding mechanics, while adding explicit medical authorization to upload, download and projection routes.

existing.name: companies + users + internal_users + shifts
existing.change: No new scalar fields. Add reverse relations for case origin, recipients, authenticated actors and affected shifts.
existing.why: Reuse business identity, recipient lookup, Ops actor identity and shift timezone. A single injury can affect shifts at several businesses; each sees only its own notice/shift projection.

flows.title: Injury intake → recovery
flows.summary: Structured reports enter directly from the existing backend. Neutron handles unstructured reports and asks Ops to confirm uncertainty.
steps: Receive report
Worker/supervisor form, Ops action, or Slack report reference.
Read Incident type, worker, company and shift. Unstructured input is classified; low-confidence stays PENDING_CONFIRMATION.
Create/reuse incidents row with stable sourceReference. No medical hold before confirmation.
Confirmed medical report reaches openOrAttachCase(incidentId, actor).
Open or attach case
Confirmed incident plus same-worker duplicate candidates from the prior 7 days.
Read existing cases; match incident identity/date/shift, not just worker+7 days. Serialize intake for this worker.
Transaction: medical_cases, incidents.medicalCaseId, CASE_OPENED/REPORT_LINKED event, initial cancel/review impacts and effects. Repeated source key reuses the result.
Worker medicalHold becomes true immediately after commit; worker home RTW task appears.
Pause upcoming shifts
CANCEL_SHIFT effects for accepted/invited slots within 48 elapsed hours.
Reread worker_shifts + shifts, actual start time and in-progress state.
Call existing cancellation service; write actual medical_case_shifts outcomes and effect result. Flag later shifts for review; alert Ops for in-progress work.
Normal cancellation downstream processing/backfill runs under its existing policy. Failures remain visible in Ops; case hold stays active.
Submit a recovery note
Owned photo/PDF, visit date, RESTRICTED/NOT_CLEARED, structured limits and expected return or unknown date.
Validate file ownership/type and local dates. Read/lock case.version; worker cannot edit a resolved injury.
Transaction: immutable medical_submissions, case RECOVERING/date projection, followUpCycle++, event, window cancellation and follow-up effects.
After commit show confirmed cancellations separately from pending cancellations. Upload never promises cancellations that have not completed.
Follow up
FOLLOW_UP effect on expected return date, or day 14 if unknown.
Read current case kind/state/cycle and whether a newer note exists. Stale job exits without messaging.
Use outreach broker for push+SMS; record outreachAttemptId. Plan +3-day reminder and +7-day Ops call todo, each anchored to the first follow-up due date.
New submission starts a new cycle; full note goes to Ops review. Case creation also starts a no-note reminder cycle.

flows.title: Full note → Ops approval → customer
flows.summary: Medical clearance and notification are separate commands. Overall account restrictions remain authoritative.
steps: Submit full clearance
Worker submits owned document, visit date and FULL with no active restrictions.
Validate against latest case version; require current injury case.
Insert medical_submissions PENDING; case PENDING_REVIEW, followUpCycle++, reviewDueAt; write event and Ops review/SLA effects.
Booking remains blocked. Worker sees the one-business-day review message.
Review note
Ops opens private case detail and chooses Approve, Reject, or Request info.
Read latest pending FULL note, prior submissions, claim status, actor permission and case version.

Approve: note APPROVED + case RESOLVED + resolvedAt + approvedSubmissionId + event/effects. Reject/info: stamp note decision/reason, case AWAITING_NOTE, invalidate cycle and schedule new upload reminders.
Decision is atomic; conflicting/stale decisions return a refresh prompt. Claim status does not change clearance.
Recompute booking eligibility
Case approval or void completed.
Check every other open injury case and the existing account/shift eligibility rules.
No account_status update; cancel stale review/reminder effects and release later-shift review flags for this case.
Worker can book only if all restrictions pass. Cancelled shifts are never automatically rebooked.
Preview customer notice
Ops chooses affected business/recipient and opens template preview.
Resolve recipients and company-scoped shifts. Check no remaining hold or account restriction before drafting a 'can return' notice.
medical_case_notices DRAFT with safePayload/template body and current preview actor/time.
Only worker name, cleared date and relevant shift details appear. No diagnosis, restrictions, note image or case timeline.
Send and reconcile
Explicit Send command with notice idempotency key.
Recheck permissions, recipient scope, current preview, overall booking eligibility and whether already queued/sent.
Transaction: notice QUEUED + SEND_CUSTOMER_NOTICE effect. Dispatcher sends; writes SENT/provider id/event or FAILED/AMBIGUOUS.
Business console shows SENT notices; failed notice stays actionable in Ops without reopening the medical hold.

flows.title: Sick cancellation → optional details
flows.summary: Cancellation completes first. The worker can add details later, without a booking block.
steps: Cancel for sickness
Worker cancels shift with SICKNESS.
Use existing cancellation checks and policy.
Existing WorkerShift cancellation commits before the optional health step.
Show optional note/return-date step; Skip leaves cancellation intact and creates no empty medical case.
Add illness details
Any of document, expected return date, or worker note; optionally later from cancelled shift.
Read worker-owned cancelled shift and linked illness case if one already exists.
Create/reuse medical_cases kind ILLNESS, medical_submissions, origin medical_case_shifts and event. File is optional.
No medicalHold. Booking before expected date shows a reminder and can continue if ordinary eligibility passes.
Handle other shifts and penalties
Worker explicitly selects other shifts before expected date; a note may arrive after the original cancellation.
Read eligible affected shifts and original cancellation strikes/reliability effects.

Enqueue selected cancellations only. A validated attached note requests medical exemption for linked sickness cancellations; run existing penalty correction and reevaluate affected policy restrictions.
Show actual cancellation/exemption result. Without note, existing cancellation policy remains in force.
Share absence notice
Ops previews absence template and chooses Send.
Read only that company's shifts, expected date and note-on-file boolean.
Use same medical_case_notices/effects as clearance; persist sender, recipient and send outcome.
Business sees the expected date as provisional, with no medical free text.
Optional document consent
Worker affirmatively shares one illness document with one named company.
Verify ownership, current ILLNESS kind and permission text version.
Insert medical_document_consents and event. Worker revoke stamps revokedAt. Business download route checks the grant every request and streams the file privately.
Business may view that one authorized file; no access to other notes, restrictions or timeline. New uploads remain private.
Convert to injury
Ops confirms a work-related cause.
Lock case, read linked shift/submissions and current consents.

Same case id becomes INJURY; link/create existing Incident, set claim NOT_FILED, revoke consents, followUpCycle++, event and initial hold/cancellation effects. Existing illness note is preserved but does not auto-clear injury.
Medical hold starts now; request complete injury/clearance input. Worker and Ops retain one continuous history.

flows.title: Retries, competing updates & failures
flows.summary: The case stays authoritative. Execution records show exactly which side effects still need attention.
steps: Two reports arrive together
Worker and AM report one event, or two distinct injuries within 7 days.
Stable source references + worker intake lock + incident identity/date/shift.
Same incident attaches to one case; distinct injury creates a second. Uncertain duplicates require Ops decision.
No auto-merge just because the worker and week match.
Approval races a new note
Ops approves an older FULL note while the worker submits a newer restricted note.
Case row lock/version and newest submission identity.
One command wins; the stale command makes no partial changes and returns conflict.
Ops refreshes before deciding; the worker is not accidentally cleared.
Cancellation or send fails
Dispatcher crashes, pipeline rejects cancellation, or provider acknowledgement is uncertain.
Effect lease, dedupeKey, actual WorkerShift state and provider reference.
Retry safe actions; surface exhausted failure. Treat uncertain outbound delivery as AMBIGUOUS for reconciliation.
No duplicate cancellations, no blind email resend, and no false 'sent' or 'cancelled' UI state.
Multiple holds or suspension
One case resolves while another injury or account restriction remains.
Derived all-case hold and existing account status at booking and send time.
Resolve only this case. No account status overwrite.
Worker sees remaining reason; Ops cannot send a misleading 'can return' notice.
No contact / unknown date / in-progress shift
Missing date, 30 days without response, or a worker already clocked in.
Current case state, follow-up cycle and actual shift times.
Unknown date uses 14-day reminder; ongoing injury remains held after 30 days until an authorized decision. Keep in-progress shift and alert Ops.
Ops owns the exception. Case closure without clearance and manual light-duty approval remain unresolved product policies.

decisions: Chosen: one medical_cases table with INJURY/ILLNESS discriminator. Separate InjuryCase + IllnessRecord was considered, but conversion would duplicate ownership, notes and sharing history.

Keep Incident as report evidence and a linked medical case as recovery state. Extending Incident alone was considered, but one case can have several reports and an illness starts from a cancelled shift rather than an incident.

Use medical_case_effects as a narrow outbox, executed by existing services. A prompt-only Neutron workflow was considered, but booking enforcement and atomic case/penalty changes belong in the backend.
Worker home card is a derived API projection. Reuse WorkerTodo for Ops tasks, without assuming those todos already render in the mobile home screen.

No standalone insurance integration, restriction-based shift matching, generic workflow framework, or new scheduler. One carrier claim per case in v1; multiple carrier claims would justify a separate table later.
questions: Named Ops owner and injury-read/review/void permissions, including whether on-sites may see medical files.
Business-day calendar, timezone and holidays for the review SLA; follow-up morning time; 14/3/7-day defaults.
Whether a same-day expected RTW cancels that entire date. This proposal includes the entire local RTW date and keeps booking blocked until approval.
Whether an unknown date is permitted. This proposal allows it explicitly to reconcile R3.2 with R4.3/R5.1; it never allows an accidental missing date.
Which customer recipient receives multi-business absence/clearance notices and whether an initial injury absence notice is mandatory.
Document retention, expiry and consent-copy policy. Injury files stay private; illness file sharing is per-document opt-in.
Handling 30-day no-contact closure or light duty. Neither can silently bypass full-clearance approval in this v1 design.
Medical exemption eligibility and retroactive reversal policy. Existing cancelled-shift penalties must be reevaluated, without removing unrelated strikes or holds.
The intended worker FAQ/help bot surface. Matrix Navi currently names an internal worker-monitoring agent; reuse of a mobile support bot still needs verification.

document.title: Injury & return to work
document.subtitle: One recovery case. Clear worker guidance. An Ops decision before returning.
document.modelIntro: Doctor visits and expected return dates use date. Submissions, decisions and scheduled execution use timestamptz. Nullable fields are marked below.
document.modelConventionsTitle: Local dates and instants are different
document.notStored: No Injured account status, no second copy of the incident report, no standalone FollowUp table, and no case-wide consent boolean. Booking hold is derived; effects schedule follow-ups; consent belongs to one document and one business.
document.flowContract:
Existing report intake / Worker app / Ops / Neutron
→ MedicalCasesModule command + authenticated actor
→ transaction: case + submission/event + shift impacts + durable effects
→ existing cancellation / jobs / outreach / todos / email delivery
→ worker projection / private Ops queue / safe business notices

flowNotes.title: The booking invariant
flowNotes.text: medicalHold = any open INJURY case. Every booking and assignment path applies this as a hard stop. Ordinary account/shift eligibility still applies after the medical hold is removed.

flowNotes.title: Neutron proposes; the backend commits
flowNotes.text: Structured medical reports call the case command directly. Slack reports go through classification and confirmation. The generic Matrix Slack trigger ignores bot posts; app emergency posts need a direct hook or the separate allowed-bot handler.

document.diagramNote: Incident reports remain the evidence. Cases own medical state. Effects call the existing services. Booking checks every open injury and the usual eligibility rules. Clearing a case and sending a customer notice are separate actions.

summary.decision: Build on the incident system we have
summary.nextAction: Add medical recovery state, enforce it in the backend, and reuse cancellation and outreach.
reuse: Incident + supervisor intake: reports, worker/shift/company links and Slack routing.
WorkerShift cancellation: cancellation side effects and policy-based backfill.
Outreach + scheduled jobs: push/SMS delivery, suppression, timing and audit.
Ops Action Center patterns: queue filters, review actions and detail navigation.
netNew: Medical case lifecycle: one record for injury or illness; in-place conversion.
Derived booking hold: all open injuries count; account restrictions remain.
Private medical-note review: immutable inputs, current-note decisions and consent.
Safe customer notices: preview, explicit send and recorded delivery outcome.
buildSequence: Case + hold + release path together: schema, confirmed intake, all-path booking enforcement, cancellation, baseline worker upload and Ops review/approve/void. Gate live holds until the full release path works.
Worker inputs + private review: richer home/history/restriction inputs, optional sick details and medical permissions.
Follow-ups + customer communication: timers, reminders, claims, preview/send, business notices, document consent and illness conversion.
